briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF S-002
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- north roof: (-82, -126), roof
- workshop: (93, 91), indoor
- workcell West: (84, -116), indoor
- antenna mast: (-56, 62), outdoor
- site B: (-22, -23), outdoor

Robots:
- A1 (fixed_arm): installed at workcell West and cannot move; it can only work on tasks located at workcell West. Equipment: robotic arm. Mains-powered (no endurance limit).
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 10 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3360 s, including the return to its start.
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 8 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg), thermal camera. Endurance: 1140 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Deliver the spare pump (2 kg) to antenna mast. Location: antenna mast. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 2 kg).
- T2: Deliver the battery pack (4 kg) to workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 4 kg).
- T3: Tighten the valve at workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 240 s. Needs: robotic arm. Can start only after T2 is finished.
- T4: Tighten the valve at workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 240 s. Needs: robotic arm.
- T5: Tighten the valve at workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 180 s. Needs: robotic arm.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 900 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Morning! Plan for today's site work:

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: north roof (-82, -126, a rooftop); workshop (93, 91, indoors); workcell West (84, -116, indoors); antenna mast (-56, 62, outside); site B (-22, -23, outside).

The fleet: A1 is a robot arm bolted down in workcell West; it can't move but can work on jobs inside workcell West, and it runs on mains power. M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 10 kg, moves at 1 m/s and lasts 56 minutes including getting back. D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera and a thermal camera; it flies at 8 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 19 minutes including the flight home.

Jobs:
(T1) Antenna mast needs the spare pump, which weighs 2 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.
(T2) Drop the battery pack off at workcell West; it weighs 4 kg - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T3) The valve at workcell West needs tightening - that takes 4 minutes on site but only once the battery pack (T2) has arrived.
(T4) The valve at workcell West needs tightening - that takes 4 minutes on site.
(T5) Someone has to tighten the valve at workcell West - that takes 3 minutes on site.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 15 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
